title: Aladdin: Joint Placement and Scaling for SLO-Aware LLM Serving
technique: cluster-level co-adaptive scheduler: predicts minimal GPUs/worker configuration for a query stream and places queries on workers using prefill/decode latency models (bin-packing-style) to maximise per-worker utilisation

optimized_metrics.evidence: our task is to determine how to use the minimum number of GPUs to serve both newly submitted and ongoing requests while ensuring compliance with the SLO requirements.
Aladdin first predicts minimal computing resources and the corresponding serving workers' configuration required to fulfill the SLOs for all queries.
we have set a predetermined response deadline for time to the first token (TTFT). ... The SLO is attained when both TTFT and ATGT latency meet the requirement.

optimized_metrics.evidence: it places the queries to each serving worker according to the prefill and decode latency models of batched LLM inference to maximize each worker's utilization.

headline_claim.text: Aladdin reduces the serving cost of a single model by up to 71% for the same SLO level compared with the baselines

reported_metrics.where: §6.4 number of GPUs required vs arrival rate (simulation)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: the first token generation is a single-round inference process without iteration, so we have set a predetermined response deadline for time to the first token (TTFT).
metric_definitions.notes: TTFT never formally defined; used as prefill-latency deadline. Table 2: 'prefill latency SLOs are the approximated inference latency for the model's context length (4096 tokens) for each testbed'

metric_definitions.definition_quote: previous work [20] adopts the time between tokens (TBT) metric, constraining the latency between every token smaller than the target. However, the TBT metric is an over-strict metric with less flexibility, and it does not directly affect the user's quality of experience.
average token generation time (ATGT) metric ATGT = t_decode / (l_out - 1), where t_decode is the decode time of a request and l_out - 1 is the output length of the decode phase.
metric_definitions.notes: = TPOT (excludes first token); per-request average; decode time excludes queueing/prefill

metric_definitions.definition_quote: The SLO is attained when both TTFT and ATGT latency meet the requirement.
we use the number of GPUs required to achieve a certain SLO attainment rate as the main metric.

slo_spec: Per-request: TTFT deadline = approx. inference latency for the full 4096-token context on each testbed; decode (ATGT) SLO chosen so batched per-token latency does not exceed 1.3x the individual-request inference latency. Evaluated as SLO attainment rate; cost = GPUs needed to hit a target attainment.
load_regime: request-rate sweep (Poisson arrivals, varying lambda); real testbed for end-to-end, large-scale simulation for GPU counts
workloads: ShareGPT_V3_unfiltered_cleaned_split prompts, Poisson arrivals; output lengths from model's generated responses (max 2048)
extractor_notes: Cost = number of GPUs (no $ cost). SLO attainment is a constraint targeted at 'all queries'; P99 ATGT is a reported metric only in real-testbed results. Builds on vLLM workers. Not primarily an in-replica scheduler (cluster placement + scaling), but cluster D1 per assignment.

tail_audit.metrics: P99 ATGT (average token gen time; reported); SLO is on mean ATGT and TTFT

load_class_quote: submit the prompts follows a Poisson distribution (§6.1); GPU counts vs arrival rate in large-scale simulation (§6.4)
